The ’90s Just Called — They Want Their DIY Fashion Trend Back

Donny MeachamPublished: September 10, 2026
  • SHARE
  • TWEET
Höre the Latest Hits
auf Amazon Music Unlimited (ad)
Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 1:58
Instaread

Something very ’90s is sneaking its way back into fashion — and you may already have a closet full of it.

The DIY trend that once ruled summer camps, school projects and sleepovers is suddenly having a major moment again, with about 1 million U.S. Google searches a month, up 20% year over year.

Even better? New sales data shows Americans aren't just searching for the nostalgic style. They're actually buying it again.

This ’90s DIY Trend Is Back

According to Free Spirited Clothing, interest has surged in 2026, with tie-dye searches reaching roughly 3.4 million in the four weeks between Feb. 8 and March 7.

READ MORE: The Top 100 Movies of the ’90s

For anyone who grew up in the ’90s, tie-dye wasn't just something you bought. You made it yourself — at summer camp, during a school project or at home with a white shirt and a questionable amount of dye.

“There's something very nostalgic about tie-dye because, for a lot of Americans, their first experience with it wasn't buying something from a store. It was making it themselves,” Abby Rafer of Free Spirited Clothing said.

Rainbow Is Still King

Tie-dye has gotten a modern makeover, with pastel, earth-tone and more understated designs now competing with the classic psychedelic look.

But Americans aren't exactly ready to calm down.

Rainbow/multi-color designs accounted for 22.51% of tie-dye purchases, making them the No. 1 choice nationwide. Blue followed at 16.90%, with green at 15.76%.

READ MORE: What It Was Like to Hang Out at the Mall in the '90s

Rainbow was also the favorite in 43 of the 46 states with enough sales data to determine a winner.

Get our free mobile app

So if you're suddenly tempted to grab a white T-shirt and start twisting it into a colorful little masterpiece, you're not alone.

The ’90s aren't done with us yet.

LOOK: 19 Drinks Only '90s Kids Remember

Grab that weird bendy straw you bought with your Chuck. E Cheese tokens, because we're sluprin' up these definitive flavors of the '90s.

Gallery Credit: Meg Dowdy

eBay

Ecto-Cooler

This Ghostbusters-inspired citrus moment first hit shelves in 1989 and was INSTANTLY adored by kids across the United States.

YouTube

Squeezit

Squeezit was basically corn syrup and Red Dye No. 40 in a thin plastic bottle that featured an absolute choking hazard of a lid. Who let us drink these things?

amazon

Lil' Hugs

Two types of people in this world
  • People who puncture the lid of a Lil' Hug with a straw
  • SAVAGES who peel off the lid and expose themselves to the textural nightmare that is the remaining glue on the lip of the Lil' Hug

eBay

Surge

SURGE walked so Monster Energy could run.

eBay

Sharkleberry Finn

Every week was Shark Week if your parents loved you enough to buy Sharkleberry Fin, the undisputed King of Kool-Aid flavors.

eBay

Crystal Pepsi

Don't get it twisted: Crystal Pepsi was not a lemon-lime soda--it was Pepsi without the caramel color added.

eBay

Clearly Canadian

Have you ever wished your La Croix could give you diabetes? Enter Clearly Canadian, the sweet carbonated treat.

eBay

Josta

Another proto-energy drink, Josta was like cola with more caffeine and Guarana for the 'boost' one needed to FINALLY advance to the final level of Super Mario Bros. 3.

eBay

Orbitz

Orbitz: for when you wanted to crack open an ice-cold lava lamp.

eBay

Jolt Cola

TWICE THE CAFFEINE FOR TWICE THE ENERGY FOR TWICE THE PEP FOR TWICE THE MOVES FOR BEING SO EXCITED, SO EXCITED, SO... SCARED?

eBay

TAB

Tell me you had an Almond Mom without telling me you had an Almond Mom.

eBay

Fruitopia

Fruitopia was doing the most to embrace the vibes of the '90s. Just look at this poster. You can almost hear Dave Matthews in the distance.

eBay

Sobe

SoBe: because lizards and other reptiles most definitely drink pina coladas.

YouTube

Mistic

Someone had the idea of making non-alcoholic wine coolers and we all fell for it. NGL: Mistic was kind of doing the most in the early '90s.

eBay

Crystal Light

Almond Mom strikes again!

eBay

Tang

Apparently, astronauts drank this powdered version of orange juice--or at least that's what our parents told us to ensure we didn't die of scurvy.

YouTube

Mondo

What was with these choking hazard lids, man? And why did everything need to be squeezable?

eBay

Gatorade

If you remember when Gatorade came in glass bottles, it's time to consider adding retinol to your skincare routine. Also: anyone who refers to a type of Gatorade by its flavor (in this case: Citrus Cooler) and not its color (Orange) is 100% a cop. They taught us that in D.A.R.E.

eBay

Purplesaurus Rex

The Kool-Aid man slayed so hard in his Jurassic Park getup that he killed the dinosaurs.
